# Music 320c \| Spring 2024

### Audio DSP Projects in Faust and C++

![](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/courses/320c/img/banner.png)

## Course Information

**Developed and maintained by:** Julius O. Smith III
( [jos](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/)), initially
with the help of Champ Darabundit (first TA)


**Prerequisites:**

- Prior programming experience in [C](https://www.learn-c.org/)/C++
- Signal processing theory, and Matlab \| Octave \| Python experience on the level of Music 320A/B

**Course Summary**

Music 320C focuses on developing audio signal-processing plugins
and stand-alone applications in C++. Prior experience is assumed with
programming in C/C++, and signal processing theory and programming
on the level of Music 320A and/or 320B. Class time is devoted
to presenting and discussing the JUCE framework for creating audio
plugins and stand-alone applications, the Faust (Functional AUdio STream)
programming language for generating audio C++, related theory and projects,
project progress reports, and project final presentations.


**Course Goals**

- Develop and further your skills in C++, git, and UNIX

- Build audio plugins and applications using the [JUCE framework](https://juce.com/)
- Use [Plugin GUI Magic](https://foleysfinest.com/developer/pluginguimagic/) to create
professional looking GUIs, saved as XML
- Build upon and apply your 320-level audio signal processing knowledge
- Learn about the [Faust programming language](https://faust.grame.fr/) and its libraries
- Your cool projects!

**Assignments**

The first several assignments get you up and running using the relevant software tools, followed by your project work.

**Grading**

Grades are based on course diligence, assignment quality,
project updates/demos, and final project work.


## Itinerary

- Introductions and Course Overview
- [**Assignments:**](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/courses/320c/index.html#assignments)
JUCE, Plugin GUI Magic, Faust Integration, Spectrum Analyzer, Filter Bank
- [**Projects:**](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/courses/320c/index.html#projects) Make a Synth, Final Project
- Project Presentations

* * *

## Assignments

The Music 320C _assignments_ cover the following basic
tools and exercises for audio plugin development:


0. Get up and running with JUCE, Plugin GUI Magic (PGM), and Projucer

1. Make a real-time spectrum analyzer plugin using the
    [`juce_dsp` module](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/juce_modules/group__juce__dsp.html)
2. Make a real-time filter-bank plugin using the Faust Libraries


In more detail, we have the following specific assignments (only 1-FFT and 2-FilterBank have deliverables):


- JUCE: [Getting Started with JUCE and the Projucer](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/courses/320c/assignments/JUCE/index.html)
- PGM: [Getting Started with Plugin GUI Magic (PGM)](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/courses/320c/assignments/PGM/index.html)
- 1-FFT: [Real-time _FFT spectrum-analyzer_ plugin using the](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/courses/320c/assignments/1-FFT/index.html) [`juce_dsp` module](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/juce_modules/group__juce__dsp.html)
- Faust: [Integrating Faust code in your JUCE plugin](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/courses/320c/assignments/Faust/index.html)
- 2-FilterBank: [Real-time _filter-bank_ plugin using Faust Libraries and\\
JUCE](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/courses/320c/assignments/2-FilterBank/index.html)

## Projects

In addition to the two assigned plugins above, we have the following plugin _projects:_

#### 1\. Synthesizer

Build on the assignments to design your own synthesizer plugin
or standalone program.

You choose the sound-synthesis
method, and the definition of "synthesizer" is flexible.


#### 2\. Final Project

Your final project is open ended and can build on prior work in the class.


## Tentative Weekly Schedule

- Tuesday is "lecture day", where concepts are introduced and discussed in class.
- The rest of the week, we asynchronously read/view course materials, complete the week's assignment, pursue project
work, and/or discuss issues or topics to share on Discord, email, Zoom, etc.

By week (subject to change):


01. JUCE
02. PGM
03. 1-FFT
04. Faust
05. 2-FilterBank
06. Synth Project
07. Synth Project Continued - talk about Final Projects
08. Final Project Updates and Discussions, Special Topics
09. Final Project Updates and Discussions, Special Topics
10. Final Project Presentations

## Your Mileage May Vary

Completing the assignments quickly leaves you more time for
your final project, and this is encouraged.

However, it
is also perfectly fine to spend most of the quarter learning
more software tools and doing a more straightforward final project.
